newsitem.title: UK: UK court puts permanent ban on Co-op papers.
newsitem.headline: UK court puts permanent ban on Co-op papers.

text.p: The London High Court on Friday granted a permanent injunction barring Andrew Regan and his bidding vehicle Galileo from using confidential information about the Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) in any takeover offer.

Regan's ambitious plan to convert the mutually-owned Co-op into a limited company and sell off some of its businesses collapsed on Thursday, after the Co-op refused to countenance Galileo's proposals.
UK court puts permanent ban on Co-op papers

The court also extended the scope of the injunction to include British investment bank Hambros, which has acted as adviser to 31-year-old entrepreneur Regan and Galileo, and awarded costs against Regan, Galileo, Regan's associate David Lyons, Regan's company Lanica Investment Trust and suspended CWS executive Allan Green.

"I regard this is a quite exceptional case (and a) gross, wilful and disgraceful breach of confidence. The order is effectively final with regard to these documents," said the judge, Mr Justice Lightman.

Bill Shannon, a spokesman for CWS, said, "We totally agree with what the judge said, I don't think he could have expressed it better. We made it clear in February that no part of the CWS was for sale. What we have seen is that our values and principles are not shared by some people in the City."

Earlier, the court was told by Christopher Clarke, representing CWS, that the documents passed to Regan and Lyons by Green had been copied or pased on to Hambros and eventually found their way into the hands of 14 other entities.
